title: Peripheral Retinal Neovascularization: An FFA Masterclass
summary: Peripheral retinal neovascularization (NVE) is a pathological response to chronic retinal ischemia, driven by the upregulation of VEGF. Fluorescein Fundus Angiography (FFA), particularly Ultra-Widefield (UWF), remains the gold standard for identifying capillary non-perfusion and the characteristic 'smoke-stack' or 'sea-fan' leakage of new vessels.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Peripheral Neovascularization (NVE) refers to the proliferation of new, fragile blood vessels arising from the retinal circulation, located at least 1 disc diameter away from the optic nerve head. These vessels lack a functional blood-retinal barrier, leading to the hallmark 'profuse leakage' seen on FFA. NVE is the hallmark of proliferative retinopathies and is a direct consequence of retinal capillary non-perfusion (CNP).

sections.title: Pathophysiological Cascade
content: 1. Chronic Retinal Capillary Non-Perfusion (Ischemia)
2. Upregulation of Hypoxia-Inducible Factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α)
3. Massive release of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF)
4. Endothelial cell proliferation and migration through the ILM
5. Formation of immature, leaky vascular tufts (NVE)
6. Fibrovascular scaffolding and vitreoretinal traction

branches: Vascular: PDR, BRVO, CRVO (Hemicentral), Ocular Ischemic Syndrome
Hematologic: Sickle Cell (SC, S-Thal), Hyperviscosity Syndromes
Inflammatory: Sarcoidosis, Eales Disease, Pars Planitis, Behcet's
Congenital/Genetic: FEVR, Coats Disease, ROP, Norrie Disease
Traumatic: Radiation Retinopathy, Scleral Buckle-induced ischemia

sections.title: FFA Imaging Protocol (Ultra-Widefield)
content: 1. Baseline red-free and autofluorescence photos.
2. Bolus injection (5ml of 10% Sodium Fluorescein).
3. Early Phase (0-30s): Identify transit time and early NVE filling.
4. Mid Phase (1-3 min): Map areas of Capillary Non-Perfusion (CNP).
5. Late Phase (5-10 min): Evaluate NVE leakage intensity and disc staining.

sections.title: Specific Entity: Sickle Cell Retinopathy
content: Stage 1: Peripheral arteriolar silver-wiring.
Stage 2: Peripheral arteriolar-venular anastomoses.
Stage 3: 'Sea-fan' neovascularization (Goldberg Class III).
Stage 4: Vitreous hemorrhage.
Stage 5: Tractional Retinal Detachment.
FFA Hallmark: Circumferential peripheral ischemia with 'Sea-fan' NV at the border of perfused and non-perfused retina.

content.explanation: S: Sickle Cell, O: Ocular Ischemic Syndrome, S: Sarcoidosis, D: Diabetes (PDR), E: Eales Disease, F: FEVR.

sections.title: Critical FFA Red Flags
content: NVD (Disc NV): High risk of rapid vision loss; requires immediate PRP.
Peripheral non-perfusion > 10 disc areas: High risk for neovascular glaucoma.
Enlarged Foveal Avascular Zone (FAZ): Signifies macular ischemia; poor visual prognosis.
Vitreous hemorrhage obscuring view: FFA may be limited; consider B-scan USG.

rows: Intravitreal injection; rapid regression of NV; 1-month intervals initially
1200-1500 burns; 200-500um size; creates 'controlled atrophy' to reduce VEGF demand
Laser only the ischemic segment identified on UWF-FFA
Removal of vitreous scaffold; endolaser; membrane peeling

sections.title: Surgical Pearl: Laser Settings
content: Laser Spot Size: 200–500 µm.
Duration: 0.1s (Standard) or 0.02s (Pattern/Pascal).
Power: Titrate to a 'creamy white' burn.
Spacing: One burn-width apart.
UWF-FFA Guidance: Use UWF images to ensure laser covers the extreme periphery and all CNP zones.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Trials
content: DRS (Diabetic Retinopathy Study): Established PRP as standard for high-risk PDR.
ETDRS: Defined NVE and the benefit of early PRP in certain cases.
Protocol S (DRCR.net): Anti-VEGF (Ranibizumab) was non-inferior to PRP for PDR at 2 years.
PANORAMA: Aflibercept can prevent progression to PDR in severe NPDR cases.

sections.title: Complications & Prognosis
content: Tractional Retinal Detachment (TRD): Due to contraction of the fibrovascular stalk.
Neovascular Glaucoma (NVG): Migration of VEGF to the anterior segment; 'Rubeosis Iridis'.
Ghost Cell Glaucoma: Secondary to long-standing Vitreous Hemorrhage.
Macular Epiretinal Membrane: Post-inflammatory or post-ischemic fibrocellular proliferation.
Prognosis: Excellent if treated early; poor if NVG or foveal-involving TRD develops.

rows: Demarcation line / Ridge in Zone I/II

content.explanation: NVE leaks into the vitreous like smoke (fluorescein plumes). If it doesn't leak, it's 'mirroring' a vessel (IRMA).

sections.title: Recent Advances: OCT-A
sections.content: Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography (OCT-A) now allows for non-invasive visualization of NVE. While limited in the far periphery compared to UWF-FFA, OCT-A can visualize the 'medusa-head' morphology of NVE tufts without dye injection, though it lacks the ability to demonstrate active 'leakage'.
